**Probably not, unless your company owns the underlying lidar data.** This is an Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN), not an open competition. NRCan intends to award the work to Airborne Imaging / Forsite (Calgary), and the notice says they are the only known supplier that meets the mandatory criteria.

**What's being bought** (CanadaBuys, Open Government Licence – Canada)
- **Notice:** NRCan-5000098113, "Open license for lidar data and data analysis" (cb-29-37893161)
- **Scope:** An open licence on existing leaf-off lidar from fall 2024 covering Calgary, Edmonton, Winnipeg and Halifax (about 6,150 km²), plus processing and analysis to meet NRCan's specifications.
- **Estimated value:** $332,100 CAD, excluding taxes. Contract period runs from about November 18, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
- **Deadline:** Statements of capabilities close Mon. November 16, 2026, 14:00 ET, which is 13 days from today.

**Why your lidar analysis expertise may not qualify**
The mandatory criteria are mostly about data ownership, not analysis skill. A supplier must:
1. Be the copyright holder and rights manager for the lidar covering each city, and be able to grant all licensing rights.
2. Offer an open licence compatible with the Open Government Licence – Canada.
3. Provide data that meets the specs: at least 20 pulses/m², non-vegetated vertical RMSE of 10 cm or better, at least 50% swath overlap, NAD83(CSRS) epoch 2010, CGVD2013 and CGG2013, LAZ format, and so on.
4. Cover at least 90% of the municipal boundaries of the four cities.

Analysis capability alone doesn't meet any of these.

**Recommendation**
- **If you don't own leaf-off lidar for those four cities:** don't spend effort bidding. You would need to demonstrate the data rights, which you likely can't do.
- **If you do own or can license-hold qualifying data:** you can challenge the ACAN by submitting a written statement of capabilities to Serge Tshimanga (serge.tshimanga@nrcan-rncan.gc.ca) before 14:00 ET on November 16. It must include documentary evidence of the data rights and specs. If a qualifying statement is received, NRCan says it will run a competitive process.

**Caveats**
- The tool read only the notice text. The notice has one amendment, which I did not review, and the solicitation documents may add requirements.
- I didn't check whether your company holds this data. That's the deciding factor, so confirm it with your team first.

**Short answer: probably not as a bid. Your only realistic move is a statement of capabilities, and only if your company owns qualifying lidar data.**

**What this notice is:** CB notice cb-29-37893161 (NRCan-5000098113) is an Advance Contract Award Notice, not an open tender. NRCan intends to award a sole-source contract (est. $332,100 CAD, Nov 18, 2026 to Mar 31, 2027) to **Airborne Imaging / Forsite** of Calgary. Other suppliers can only block the award by submitting a statement of capabilities that shows they meet every mandatory requirement.

**Deadline:** Mon Nov 16, 2026, 14:00 ET, which is 13 days from today.

**The mandatory requirements are about data, not analysis:**
- You must be the copyright holder and rights manager for high-density (≥20 pulses/m²) leaf-off lidar from 2024 or later. The data must be licensable under the Open Government Licence – Canada.
- It must cover the Calgary, Edmonton, Winnipeg and Halifax areas (about 6,150 km² in total) and cover at least 90% of each city's municipal boundaries.
- It must meet the spec: 10 cm vertical RMSE, 50% swath overlap, NAD83(CSRS) and CGVD2013 datums, LAS 1.4 point format 6 compressed to LAZ, and so on.

Lidar analysis capability alone doesn't meet these criteria. Unless you already hold data like this, you can't meet the bar, and the notice itself says Airborne/Forsite is the only known supplier that does.

**Recommendation:**
1. **Don't prepare a bid.** There is no open competition to bid on at this stage.
2. **Check your data holdings this week.** If your company holds or can license a 2024+ leaf-off dataset that meets every spec above for all four cities, submit a statement of capabilities with documentary evidence before the deadline. That is the only way to trigger a competitive process.
3. If you don't hold that data, consider a different route: contact the buyer, Serge Tshimanga (serge.tshimanga@nrcan-rncan.gc.ca), or watch for the follow-on competitive process if one is triggered. Your lidar analysis services could fit a subcontract with the data holder, if that is ever relevant to you.

**Limits of this read:** I only have the notice text. The solicitation documents aren't attached, so I can't confirm evaluation criteria or any security requirements beyond what's written here. The notice shows no security clearance requirement, but that is "not stated," not confirmed as none.

Source: CanadaBuys tender notices, Open Government Licence – Canada.

**The mandatory criteria are the problem.** Your statement must show that you:

2. Can offer an open licence compatible with the Open Government Licence – Canada.
3. Can deliver data meeting the specs: pulse density of at least 20/m², vertical RMSE of 10 cm or better, at least 50% swath overlap, NAD83(CSRS) and CGVD2013 datums, LAS 1.4 / LAZ format, and UTM-zone tiling.

- If you do qualify, send a detailed statement of capabilities with evidence to the contact before 14:00 ET on 16 Nov. A sufficient statement triggers a competitive process with technical and financial evaluation, per section 5 of the notice.
